subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 5
intro: You may use a calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong. Round only at the end, and give answers to the accuracy the question asks for.

questions.q: What is the largest integer that satisfies 5x + 2 < 30?
questions.ms: B1: 5. 5x < 28 so x < 5.6, and the largest integer below 5.6 is 5.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (3x − 2)2.
questions.ms: B1: 9x² − 12x + 4. (3x − 2)(3x − 2) = 9x² − 6x − 6x + 4. Common mistake: 9x² + 4 (missing the middle terms).

questions.q: A quadratic curve crosses the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 6. What is the x-coordinate of its turning point?
questions.ms: B1: 2. The turning point is halfway between the roots: (−2 + 6) ÷ 2 = 2.

questions.q: x is an integer. List all the values of x such that −8 ≤ 3x + 4 < 20.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3

questions.q:
A lift can carry at most 800 kg. Five people are already inside. They weigh 72.5 kg, 81 kg, 64.8 kg, 90.2 kg and 77 kg.
A worker wants to add n boxes that each weigh 24 kg.
Write an inequality in terms of n to show this information.
questions.ms: Answer: 385.5 + 24n ≤ 800. M1 for the total 385.5 kg. A1 for the inequality (must be ≤).

questions.q: Work out the greatest number of boxes the worker can add.
questions.ms: Answer: 17 boxes. M1 for 24n ≤ 414.5. M1 for n ≤ 17.27… A1 for 17 (round down: 18 boxes would go over 800 kg).

questions.q:
A square has sides of length (2x − 3) cm. Its perimeter is at least 30 cm and less than 50 cm.
x is an integer. Find all the possible values of x.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: 6, 7. M1 for 30 ≤ 4(2x − 3) < 50 or 30 ≤ 8x − 12 < 50. M1 for 5.25 ≤ x < 7.75. A1 for 6 and 7 only.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (2x + 1)(x − 3)(x + 2).
questions.ms: Answer: 2x³ − x² − 13x − 6. M1 for expanding two brackets, e.g. (2x + 1)(x − 3) = 2x² − 5x − 3. M1 for multiplying by the third bracket with at least 4 correct terms out of 6 (2x³ + 4x² − 5x² − 10x − 3x − 6). A1 cao.

questions.q: Factorise 10x2 − 11x − 6.
questions.ms: Answer: (5x + 2)(2x − 3). M1 for 10x² − 15x + 4x − 6, or brackets that give two of the three terms. A1. Check: a × c = −60, and −15 × 4 = −60, −15 + 4 = −11.

questions.q: Factorise fully 8x2 − 18.
questions.ms: Answer: 2(2x − 3)(2x + 3). M1 for 2(4x² − 9). A1 for the difference of two squares step.

questions.q: Solve 4x2 + 4x − 3 = 0 by factorising.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 1/2,-3
questions.ms: Answer: x = 1/2 or x = −3/2. M1 for 4x² + 6x − 2x − 3 or (2x − 1)(2x + 3). M1 for setting each bracket to 0. A1 for both (0.5 and −1.5 also accepted).

questions.q: Solve x(x + 5) = 4(x + 5). Give all the solutions.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = −5 or x = 4. M1 for (x + 5)(x − 4) = 0 or x² + x − 20 = 0. M1 for factorising. A1 for both. Dividing by (x + 5) gives only x = 4: max M1 A0.

questions.q:
Solve 3x2 + 4x − 9 = 0. Give your answers correct to 2 decimal places.
x = −b ± √(b2 − 4ac)2a
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 1.19 or x = −2.52. M1 for correct substitution (a = 3, b = 4, c = −9). M1 for √124 or 11.13… A1 for both answers.

questions.q:
Harriet uses the quadratic formula to solve an equation of the form ax2 + bx + c = 0. She correctly writes
x = 3 ± √(9 + 40)4
Find the values of a, b and c, and write down Harriet's equation.

A ball is kicked upwards. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is h = 25t − 4.9t2.
Find the maximum height of the ball. Give your answer to 1 decimal place. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 31.9 m. M1 for the ball landing at t = 25 ÷ 4.9 = 5.10… M1 for the top at t = 2.55… (halfway). A1 for 31.9 (accept 31.8 to 31.9).

questions.q: For how long is the ball at least 20 m above the ground? Give your answer to 2 decimal places. (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 3.12 seconds. M1 for 4.9t² − 25t + 20 = 0. M1 for correct substitution into the quadratic formula. A1 for t = 0.99… and t = 4.11… A1 for 3.12 (accept 3.11 to 3.12).

questions.q:
A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 8 m wide. A path x m wide goes all the way round the garden. The total area of the garden and path is 165 m2.
Show that 4x2 + 40x − 69 = 0.
questions.ms: M1 for (12 + 2x) and (8 + 2x). M1 for (12 + 2x)(8 + 2x) = 165 expanded to 96 + 40x + 4x² = 165. A1 for 4x² + 40x − 69 = 0 (every step shown).

questions.q: Solve 4x2 + 40x − 69 = 0 to find the width of the path. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 1.5 m. M1 for correct substitution into the formula, or (2x − 3)(2x + 23) = 0. A1 for x = 1.5 and x = −11.5. A1 for choosing 1.5 m and rejecting −11.5 because a width cannot be negative.

questions.q:
The curve y = −x2 + 2x + 15 is drawn.
Find the x-coordinates where the curve crosses the x-axis.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 5 and x = −3. M1 for −(x² − 2x − 15) = 0 or (5 − x)(x + 3) = 0. A1 for both.

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the turning point of the curve.
questions.ms: Answer: (1, 16). M1 for x = 1 (halfway between −3 and 5). A1 for y = −1 + 2 + 15 = 16.

questions.q: Is the turning point a maximum or a minimum?
questions.ms: B1: Maximum. The x² term is negative, so the curve is an upside-down U (∩ shape).

questions.q: Solve 2x2 + 9x − 18 > 0
questions.hint: Type it like x<-2 or x>4
questions.ms: Answer: x < −6 or x > 1.5. M1 for (2x − 3)(x + 6). A1 for critical values 1.5 and −6. M1 for choosing the outside regions (U-shaped curve is above the x-axis outside its roots). A1 for x < −6 or x > 1.5.

questions.q: Prove that the sum of the squares of any two consecutive integers is always odd.
questions.ms: M1 for n² + (n + 1)². M1 for 2n² + 2n + 1. A1 for 2(n² + n) + 1 with a statement: 2(n² + n) is even, so adding 1 makes it odd. Numerical examples only: 0 marks.

questions.q:
Sami says: “n2 + n is always odd, for any whole number n.”
Show that Sami is wrong, and prove what is always true about n2 + n.
questions.ms: B1 for a counter-example, e.g. n = 2 gives 6, which is even. M1 for n² + n = n(n + 1). A1 for explaining that n and n + 1 are consecutive, so one of them is even, so the product is always even.
